basis: Sensorineural deafness and skin/hair pigmentation abnormalities define WS2; iris heterochromia does not impair vision. Renal and intestinal abnormalities are occasional.
Disorder of superficial fascia and subcutaneous tissue, covered by the dermatologic axis.
Seckel syndrome features primary microcephaly, intellectual disability and skeletal growth abnormalities; additional ocular and dental defects lack established frequencies.
Hypoplastic thumbs and spinal skeletal deformities define the syndrome alongside Mullerian aplasia; reproductive tract aplasia has no axis.
Rubella-associated infectious or postinfectious inflammation of the brain.
Primary neuronal channelopathy with small-fibre neuropathy reported in 80-99%; episodic erythema and warmth do not establish skin or vascular damage.
Defined by cerebral gigantism together with jaw-bone cysts and a basal-cell naevus syndrome; no additional common organ damage established.
Shigella directly infects and inflames the colon. Dehydration and electrolyte shifts are acute consequences; extraintestinal organ injury is uncommon.
Disseminated Candida infection; individual organ sites vary, with none established here as affected in >=30%. Bloodstream infection alone is not a blood-cell disorder.
Arterial-venous malformation in the maxillofacial region; associated dental, ocular and ear symptoms do not establish common direct damage to those organs.
Seizures 11/12 with brain malformations; cardiomyopathy and liver failure 30-79%. Renal dysplasia (30-79%) and muscle injury also qualify but exceed the cap.
Urea-cycle defect; hyperammonemic brain dysfunction with ataxia and altered consciousness characterizes symptomatic adult disease (~30%+); cerebral edema may occur.
Across the 10q duplication spectrum, developmental impairment and limb/skeletal malformations predominate; other organ defects vary substantially by duplicated interval.
Autoimmune inflammation directly affects the renal glomeruli.
Acquired distal tubular acidification failure defines both renal dysfunction and an acid-base disorder; underlying diseases are not inherited as organ labels.
Lysosomal storage causes renal, cardiac and small-fibre nerve damage in most classic cases. Angiokeratomas and frequent cochlear/GI involvement omitted by cap; corneal deposits often harmless.
Malignant ovarian teratoma containing thyroid-type tissue; ovarian tumour origin has no axis. Thyrotoxicosis is uncommon and does not establish native thyroid damage.
Compensatory parathyroid overactivity from nonrenal causes; skeletal injury depends on cause and duration and is not established in >=30% across this group.
Inherited coagulation disorder causing hypercoagulability; thrombosis and osteonecrosis are variable downstream complications without established >=30% organ injury.
Reduced red-cell mass with normal red-cell volume; no other organ injury is intrinsic to this anemia category.
Autoimmune-associated pulmonary syndrome defined by reduced lung volumes and restrictive ventilatory dysfunction; additional systemic disease manifestations are separate.
Inherited cerebral small-vessel arteriopathy with defining subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy; incontinence is neurologic rather than direct urinary tract injury.
Localized aneurysmal abnormality of perifoveal retinal vessels with exudation; both retinal and vascular pathology define the lesion.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease with defining neurodegeneration; blindness reported in 30-79%. Cardiomyopathy and hearing loss are annotated at 5-29%, so excluded.
Primary microcephaly with cortical developmental abnormalities and intellectual disability; hearing loss in one reported patient does not establish >=30% involvement.
